name: Tazarotenic acid
lead: Tazarotenic acid is the active metabolite of tazarotene, a prescription topical retinoid. Tazarotene is a prodrug: after it is applied to the skin, esterase enzymes rapidly remove its ethyl ester group, producing the free acid that binds retinoic acid receptors [4][8][12]. It is not sold as a separate product; people encounter it through tazarotene (brands such as Tazorac, Arazlo and Fabior) [12].

Tazarotenic acid binds retinoic acid receptors (RARs) but not retinoid X receptors, and in laboratory assays it is selective for the RAR-beta and RAR-gamma subtypes [1][4]. Tazarotene is approved in the United States for acne, plaque psoriasis and, in some formulations, photodamage, and it is contraindicated in pregnancy [12].

In forum discussion, tazarotene is sometimes described as a stronger alternative to tretinoin for skin texture and anti-aging. No published study has tested tazarotenic acid as a stand-alone cosmetic ingredient; the human evidence concerns the parent drug.

paras: Tazarotene belongs to the acetylenic retinoids, a class whose structure resists isomerization. Its free acid, tazarotenic acid, binds RARs and not RXRs, and gene-activation assays indicate selectivity for the RAR-beta and RAR-gamma subtypes [1][4]. Through these receptors it is described as slowing keratinocyte proliferation and promoting differentiation, and reviews also discuss comedolytic and anti-inflammatory properties of topical retinoids [7][12].

After topical application, only a few percent of the dose reaches the stratum corneum and viable epidermis, and a review of the drug's pharmacokinetics describes limited absorption into the bloodstream, with less than about 6% of the applied dose absorbed [2][5]. Tazarotene is converted by esterases in human blood and liver to tazarotenic acid [8]. Tazarotenic acid is then further metabolized, with cytochrome P450 2C8 and flavin-containing monooxygenases implicated in humans [6]. Over 99% is bound to plasma proteins and it is eliminated in urine and feces [12].
No studies found of tazarotenic acid administered on its own. Human trials have tested its parent drug, tazarotene.

In a 24-week double-blind trial of 563 people with facial photodamage, followed by a 28-week open-label extension, 0.1% tazarotene cream produced significantly more improvement than vehicle in fine wrinkling, mottled hyperpigmentation, lentigines and other signs; improvement had not plateaued by week 52. Twenty of 283 tazarotene-treated participants and 1 of 280 vehicle participants stopped because of adverse events, and plasma tazarotenic acid stayed at or below 0.71 ng/mL [3]. Pooled results of two vehicle-controlled trials examined 0.1% tazarotene cream in facial acne [9]. Registered trials have also looked at tazarotene in cutaneous T-cell lymphoma and scalp psoriasis [11][13].

Skin irritation (redness, itching, burning) is the most commonly reported effect of tazarotene and tends to rise with concentration [12]. A review of tazarotene safety concluded that systemic exposure is minimal and found no association with contact sensitization, phototoxicity or carcinogenicity [5]. Tazarotene is nonetheless labelled as contraindicated in pregnancy, a position based on animal studies [12].
Researchers have developed nanoparticle formulations of tazarotene intended to deliver it to hair follicles in inflammatory skin disease [10].

timeline.event: Tazarotene described in the literature as a receptor-selective retinoid whose acid form binds RARs [1].
Tazarotene creams approved; later foam (2012) and lotion (2019) [12].

lore.intro: Tazarotenic acid is rarely named in community discussion; posts focus on tazarotene itself as a potent prescription retinoid for skin texture and aging.

claims.claim: Tazarotene is a stronger anti-aging retinoid than tretinoin
claims.believers: Proponents of prescription retinoids describe tazarotene as more potent, citing its receptor selectivity.
claims.experts: Trials show tazarotene improves photodamage versus vehicle [3]; no head-to-head comparison with tretinoin was found among the published studies reviewed.

claims.claim: The metabolite is where the activity comes from
claims.believers: Users reading drug references note that tazarotene is a prodrug.
claims.experts: Pharmacology studies confirm that esterases convert tazarotene to tazarotenic acid, which binds RARs [4][8].

card.summary: The active acid form of prescription tazarotene; evidence exists for the parent retinoid's photoaging effect, not for the metabolite alone.
card.aka: Active metabolite of tazarotene (Tazorac, Arazlo, Fabior)
card.note: Parent drug is contraindicated in pregnancy; irritation is common.

quick.overview:
Tazarotenic acid is what the body makes from tazarotene, a prescription topical retinoid used for acne, psoriasis and photodamage. It is not sold on its own.

A 12-month trial of tazarotene cream showed improvement in wrinkles and pigmentation versus vehicle. No studies have tested the acid alone.
quick.mechanism: Skin and blood esterases convert tazarotene to tazarotenic acid, which binds retinoic acid receptors, selectively RAR-beta and RAR-gamma, altering keratinocyte growth and differentiation.
quick.risks: Irritation is the most common effect of the parent drug. It is contraindicated in pregnancy. Prescription-only in the US.
